explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/534: the largest A ⊆ {1,…,N} containing N with gcd(a,b) > 1 for all a ≠ b ∈ A; Erdős' refined conjecture, proved by Ahlswede–Khachatrian, says that for N = q₁^{k₁}⋯q_r^{k_r} the maximum is attained, for some j, by the integers in [1,N] divisible by at least one of 2q₁,…,2q_j, q₁⋯q_j. IsAdmissible encodes A ⊆ [1,N], N ∈ A, pairwise gcd > 1; maxCard is the maximum size; ahlswedeKhachatrian N q is exactly the multiples in [1,N] of 2p (p a prime factor of N with p ≤ q) or of the product of those primes, so q = q_j indexes j. The statement for N ≥ 2: some prime factor q gives an admissible AK set whose size equals maxCard. This captures the resolved conjecture (the AK set is admissible and optimal). Faithful.
